subtype: Approach: staying calm and thinking where he usually puts it [Thinking]
passage: Monday. Hemant came home from school and could not find his house key. He tipped out his bag and ran up and down the stairs, and his sister Simran waited on the step, tapping her foot. Wednesday. The key was gone again. This time Hemant took a deep breath. "Where do I keep it?" he said. He checked the hook by the door, and then the shoe rack. He looked inside his shoe, and the key was there. Friday. He hung it on the hook the moment he came in and told Simran, "First breathe, then look."

qa.q: Where did Hemant find his house key on Wednesday?
qa.a: He found it inside his shoe.

qa.q: What was Hemant feeling on Monday when he ran up and down the stairs?
qa.a: He was panicked and flustered. He tipped out his bag and ran about instead of thinking, while his sister waited.

qa.q: What other approach could Hemant use so the key is easy to find, and why?
qa.a: He could hang the key on the hook the moment he comes in. Then it is always in the place he would look.

qa.q: How might Simran feel on Monday while waiting on the step?
qa.a: Simran is probably impatient and a bit annoyed, since she tapped her foot. On Friday she hears a calmer plan.

grounding: A child takes a deep breath and thinks about where he usually keeps his house key, checks the hook and the shoe rack, and finds it inside his shoe.

subtype: Approach: staying calm and thinking where he usually puts it [Thinking]
passage: Farhan, you lose your keys every week, so listen to your old Dadu Jagdish. When I was eleven, I was the one who let my little sister in after school. One day I stood at our door in Nagpur, and the key wasn't in my pocket. Chhoti started to cry. My heart was pounding, but I took one long breath and asked myself: where do I always keep it? On the hook inside the window. I reached through the bars: empty. Next, the shoe rack by the door, where I sat each morning. I lifted my old canvas shoe, and the key clinked out of the toe. Chhoti stopped crying mid-sob.

qa.q: Where did young Jagdish find the key?
qa.a: It clinked out of the toe of the old canvas shoe on the shoe rack.

qa.q: Why did young Jagdish take one long breath?
qa.a: His heart was pounding and Chhoti was crying, so he felt panicky, and the breath helped him calm down enough to think.

qa.q: Which choice in the story made the difference, and why?
qa.a: Stopping to ask where he always kept the key; it gave him two sensible places to check instead of a frantic search.

qa.q: What was the lost key like for Chhoti?
qa.a: Chhoti was stuck outside and scared enough to cry, and stopped mid-sob the moment the key appeared.

grounding: Shows a boy calming himself with a breath, thinking where he normally keeps the house key, and finding it inside his shoe on the rack.

subtype: Approach: staying calm and thinking where he usually puts it [Thinking]
passage: Rain was pouring off the stairwell roof, Akash was soaked, and the flat door wouldn't open without the key. His phone had died at lunch. Parveen Aunty from next door peered out. "Lost it, beta?" Akash wanted to kick the door. Instead he pressed his back to the wall and breathed in slowly. "Where do I always put it?" he said aloud. "The hook in my bag. Or the shoe rack, if I came home and went out again." The bag hook was empty. He bent to the rack by the door and tipped up his football boots. The key dropped out of the left one. Akash laughed out loud.

qa.a: His phone had died at lunch.

qa.q: What was Akash feeling when he wanted to kick the door?
qa.a: He felt frustrated and stressed, soaked by the rain and locked out.

qa.q: What else could Akash do to avoid getting locked out?
qa.a: Keep the key in one fixed place, like the bag hook, every time; staying calm and thinking of his usual spots found it quickly.

qa.q: How might Parveen Aunty see the way Akash handled it?
qa.a: Parveen Aunty came out expecting trouble, and would probably be impressed that he calmed down and found it himself.

grounding: Illustrates a boy breathing slowly, thinking aloud about where he normally puts his key, and finding it inside his boot on the rack.
